title: Why Does Cinema Popcorn Cost Ten Dollars?
request: Make a video on this for whats the catch
sources: AMC Entertainment Holdings, Form 10-K annual report for 2025 (filed 2026). Film costs were 48.1% of ticket revenue for the year; in the US, food and drink costs were 18.1% of snack revenue, and snack spending per visitor rose to $8.57. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411579/000141157926000016/amc-20251231x10k.htm

CNN Money, small business Q&A on running a movie theater (2002). A cinema equipment company president says the studio might take 70 to 80 percent in a film's opening week, shrinking to about 35 percent by the fifth or sixth week. https://money.cnn.com/2002/03/08/smbusiness/q_movies/

ABC News, "What Does a Trip to the Movies Really Cost You?" (2014). A California cinema owner says the corn for a large bag costs about 8 cents, a tub about 92 cents with the corn, and that he pipes the popcorn smell into the auditorium. https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/lifestyle/2014/03/what-does-a-trip-to-the-movies-really-cost-you-2/

KTLA (via KRQE), "$70 for a popcorn bucket? Movie theaters are seeing big business with blockbuster collectables" (2026). A large bucket costs a cinema under $2 to serve and sells for about $10. https://www.krqe.com/entertainment-news/70-for-a-popcorn-bucket-movie-theaters-are-seeing-big-business-with-blockbuster-collectables/amp/
The Numbers, Domestic Theatrical Market Summary for 2025. Average ticket price in the US and Canada was $11.31. https://www.the-numbers.com/market/2025/summary
Worked out from the figures above: 30% of an $11.31 ticket is about $3.40; 82% of a $10 bucket is about $8.20; $10 shared by two is $5 each.

Checked by Claude on 2026-10-15: $11.31 against The Numbers 2025 summary; $8.57 (US markets), film costs 48.1% of admissions (consolidated) and food and drink costs about 18.1% of food and drink revenue (US) against AMC's results for the full year 2025 (8-K exhibit 99.1, 23 February 2026, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411579/000141157926000018/amc-20260223xex99d1.htm). The CNN, ABC and KTLA figures are as given in Biku's script and were not opened.
